_comment: Corpus manifest for tests/roundtrip/test_roundtrip.py (issue #49).
Every number below is a PUBLISHED fact of the corresponding walkthrough: it is
either asserted by that walkthrough's check.py or recorded in an artifact the
walkthrough ships (artifacts/*.txt, artifacts/*.json, guide.html, MANIFEST.json).
Nothing here was measured into existence by this test suite -- the 'source' field
of each entry names where each group of numbers comes from, and entries omit any
fact their walkthrough does not publish rather than inventing one.
Fields:
netlist         path relative to the repository root (the canonical netlist of
the walkthrough; 04/06/10 keep theirs in a netlist/ subdirectory)
gates           total gate count as HAL sees it -- note this is the .vo instance
count plus the two synthesized constant drivers HAL_GND/HAL_VCC
gate_types      full gate-type histogram
ff              number of gates with the 'ff' GateTypeProperty
nets            total net count                    (omitted where unpublished)
global_inputs   number of global input nets        (omitted where unpublished)
global_outputs  number of global output nets       (omitted where unpublished)
global_input_names / global_output_names           (only where asserted by name)
sccs            sizes of the strongly connected components of the *gate* graph
that have more than one vertex, descending
(omitted where the walkthrough publishes no gate-level SCC)

01_blinky_counter.source: check.py asserts the histogram (l.55), the port lists (l.60-61) and the 24 size-2 SCCs (l.98/104/114); gates=50 and nets=74 from artifacts/step_stats.json; SCCs corroborated by artifacts/step_scc.json

02_traffic_fsm.source: check.py asserts the primitive split 8 ff / 14 lcell (l.57); gates=24, nets=27, the full histogram and the 3/3 port counts from guide.html and artifacts/*/findings.json
02_traffic_fsm.omitted: sccs -- 02 publishes an SCC of the flip-flop dependency graph (one non-trivial component of 8 flops, check.py l.238), not of the gate graph, so no gate-level SCC invariant is asserted here

03_uart_tx.source: check.py asserts 18 ff / 22 lcell (l.55, l.57); gates=42, nets=53, 11 inputs / 2 outputs and the full histogram from artifacts/01_stats.txt; gate SCCs [19,2,2] from artifacts/03_gate_sccs.txt and artifacts/analysis.json ('gate_sccs')

04_pwm_generator.source: check.py asserts 18 lcell / 16 ff (l.85-86); gates=36, nets=56 and the full histogram from artifacts/07_summary.json and artifacts/01_stats.txt; 14 inputs / 2 outputs from artifacts/01_stats.txt; 8 SCCs of size 2 from artifacts/05_scc.txt

05_lfsr_prng.source: check.py asserts tennm_ff==16, tennm_lcell_comb==17 and that no other type outside {tennm_ff, tennm_lcell_comb, HAL_GND, HAL_VCC} occurs (l.206-211); artifacts/scc.txt publishes 'netlist graph: 35 vertices' and 'strongly connected components of size >= 2: [25]', which together with the asserted 16/17 pins HAL_GND and HAL_VCC at 1 each
05_lfsr_prng.omitted: nets, global_inputs, global_outputs -- 05 publishes no net or port counts

06_accumulator_alu.source: check.py asserts 22 lcell / 9 ff and that no other primitive type occurs (l.69-72); gates=33, nets=53, 12 inputs / 10 outputs and the full histogram from artifacts/01_stats.txt; the 8 multi-gate SCCs of size 3 from artifacts/06_scc.txt

08_shift_debouncer.source: check.py asserts the full histogram (l.261-262), the port lists (l.265-266) and the gate-graph SCC sizes [8, 2] (l.284-285); nets=19 from artifacts/01_stats.txt and artifacts/analysis.json

10_crc8_checker.source: check.py asserts tennm_ff==8, tennm_lcell_comb==5 (l.51-53) and that exactly one SCC of size >= 8 exists (l.67-69); gates=15, nets=19, 4 inputs / 9 outputs, the full histogram and the exact SCC size 11 from artifacts/re_walk.txt and artifacts/re_walk.json
